body:
Depends on #40496, #40489, #40529

closes #31621

## Problem

Directory buffers are currently opened by the built-in browser before
`filetype=directory` is set, so other directory browsers cannot handle the
`FileType` event first, per [this comment](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/39723#issuecomment-4804095389).

## Solution

Set `filetype=directory` when Nvim detects a local directory buffer.

comment_data.body:
For this to be useful it probably should be more of a core feature, no? 

Then dir.lua can drop its `BufEnter` and `VimEnter` handlers, and simply listen for `FileType directory`.

The tricky part is that legacy dir browsers won't be using this for awhile. Not sure if that matters or if we can deal with the overlap.

Proposal:

- by default, core will "take over" this role, and if users want to use legacy dir browsers (oil.nvim etc) then they need to opt-out somehow.
- ~~Nvim should throw an error if more than one `FileType directory` handler is defined globally.~~
    - edit: that won't work bc then users can't do custom config on `FileType directory`

+To replace the built-in browser, handle the `FileType` event for "directory"

ANyways, I (re-) marked this PR as ready since (I think) it addresses your first point in isolation.

Tests fail by choosing to registering a `BufEnter` autocmd. For example, `tests_exists_autocmd.vim` asserts that there's no `BufEnter` autocmd [here](https://github.com/barrettruth/neovim/blob/f802999ddcfa16450385d493ef0c10857fab2eb8/test/old/testdir/test_exists_autocmd.vim#L4-L10), which no longer is true.

I couldn't find any other big BufEnter autocmds in the entire codebase. This strikes me as a new pattern, so let me know how you want me to move forward here: update the tests or... I'm just not doing what you were looking for XD
I've used `BufEnter` so far since the directory viewer has to fire for `:edit <dir>`, which AFAIK doesn't trigger `Buf{Read,NewFile}`.
Ah yes. Then `BufNew`? Setting filetype on `BufEnter` still looks pretty strange to me.

`BufNew` seems to behave weirdly for something like `:badd <dir>`. What do you think about  moving the filetype assignment out of the autocmd and into the core directory editing path in C and setting `filetype=directory` then?

This changes the core assumption of the directory plugin: `filetype=directory` is not a core classification.

Not loving any of these autocmd events.

> What do you think about moving the filetype assignment out of the autocmd and into the core directory editing path in C and setting `filetype=directory`

That's what I assume will be needed. Otherwise there's too many layers, not  reliable/intuitive mechanism for users/plugin-authors
oh wait, should `vim.filetype` set the filetype ?
Yep, just put up #40529. knew this discussion was too in the weeds... thank you!
